subject: SDLC artifact vouch: CI assertions, key handoff & sample logs
messages:
From: Alice Keller <alice.keller@veridianbank.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: security-team@veridianbank.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: artifacts to vouch SDLC controls for SOC2/SIG

Marcus / Redwood team,

We’re in the middle of our control evidence review and need a short bundle that demonstrates how you enforce code review and CI gating, how keystore rotation is handled, and a few sampled CI logs showing the gating behavior. Specifically:
- A short description of the PR/merge gate policy (who can approve, protected branch rules).
- One sanitized CI run showing a failed and then successful gating flow (so we can see the check sequence).
- Keystore rotation history for the last 12 months (who rotated, change tickets).
- Confirmation that no plaintext secrets are stored in repositories (either scan report or attestation).

Can you provide the artifacts by EOD 2027-07-21? If you need to redact IP or customer data, that’s fine as long as the gating steps and timestamps remain intact. If there’s an internal attestation we can rely on (signed by an engineering manager), please include it.

Thanks,
Alice Keller
Security Assurance
Veridian Bank

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Alice Keller <alice.keller@veridianbank.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: artifacts to vouch SDLC controls for SOC2/SIG

Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We can put together a compact bundle that meets your points. Plan below and what we’ll attach:

1) Merge gate policy (text + policy extract) — will include branch protection config and a short operator list showing required approvers. Attachment: merge-gate-policy.txt
2) CI run sample — sanitized pipeline log with a failing lint step followed by the author addressing comments and the pipeline completing green. Attachment: ci-run-sample-20270707.log
3) Keystore rotation timeline — CSV export of rotation events (redacted to user ids) plus change ticket references. Attachment: keystore-rotation-timeline-2026-2027.csv
4) Secrets scan / attestation — we will include the most recent repo-scan summary and an attestation PDF signed by my manager confirming no plaintext keys present. Attachment: sdlc-vouch-attestation-marcus.pdf

We’ll also add a short readme describing where each artifact came from and the exact filtering/redaction we applied. Note: for any ticket IDs that reference internal customer names we will redact and provide ticket IDs only.

Target delivery: draft bundle by 2027-07-19 for your review, final by 2027-07-21. If you need faster turnaround on any single item (e.g., the CI run), tell us which one and we’ll prioritize.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Manager, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, Alice Keller <alice.keller@veridianbank.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: artifacts to vouch SDLC controls for SOC2/SIG

Adding a few technical clarifications so the sample bundle answers the assessor’s questions directly:

- PR/merge gate: We enforce branch protection on main with required status checks: unit-tests, lint, security-scan, and license-check. The repo uses CODEOWNERS; at least one approver from the CODEOWNERS list + CI passing is required. We will include the exact branch protection JSON export.

- CI gating behavior: The sanitized CI log will show the sequence: checkout -> install -> unit tests (fail) -> author pushes fix -> CI re-run -> all checks pass -> merge. We’ll annotate the log with the step names and timestamps. The CI system rotates ephemeral runners nightly; runner identity and timestamp are included in the log.

- Keystore rotation: Keys are stored in our KMS (customer-managed for private deployments). Rotation events are recorded in our secrets audit service; the CSV will include event timestamp, operator (redacted), KMS key id (truncated), and ticket reference. We rotate service keys quarterly and rotate deployment ephemeral tokens every 24 hours.

- No-plaintext confirmation: We will include a repo-scan summary (SCA & secret-scan) and a short signed attestation. For extra confidence we can also provide the scan command + hash of the scanner binary used so you can reproduce.

I’ll prepare the runbook excerpt that explains emergency key replacement steps and link it in the readme. Expect the first draft in the Drive folder linked below.

— Irene (on behalf of Platform Controls)

From: Alice Keller <alice.keller@veridianbank.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: security-team@veridianbank.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: artifacts to vouch SDLC controls for SOC2/SIG

Marcus / Irene — appreciate the rapid plan. Two follow-ups before you assemble the bundle:

1) Please ensure one of the artifacts includes a short statement (signed/initialed by an engineering manager) explicitly confirming that secret material is not checked into git in plaintext. A brief attestation is fine.
2) Can you also include a single example ticket (redacted) showing the authorization flow for a key rotation (who approved it and the review note)? If you can’t include the full ticket, a screenshot with redactions is acceptable.

We’d like to review the draft by COB Monday (2027-07-19). If that’s tight, confirm which deliverable might slip. Thanks again — this set will be used for our SOC 2 evidence and a SIG follow-up.

Regards,
Alice
Security Assurance
Veridian Bank
